title: Exploratory pilot study to evaluate the technical feasibility of using microneedle patches for the measurement of cutaneous biomarkers
summary:
This exploratory pilot study investigates whether a newly developed microneedle patch can technically detect biomarkers and other parameters from the skin. Microneedles are very small needles designed to penetrate only the superficial layers of the skin and to provide access to skin interstitial fluid.
The patch will first be tested in up to 10 healthy adult volunteers. If the application proves technically feasible and sufficiently well tolerated, the study may then be extended to patients with atopic dermatitis and patients with chronic ulcers. The patch will be applied once for approximately two hours and will then be removed. The application site will subsequently be assessed by a physician.
The sole purpose of the study is to determine whether technically evaluable sensor signals can be obtained. The measurements will not be used for diagnosis or treatment decisions.

interventions.name: In the first study phase, the microneedle patch will be applied once to clinically unaffected skin of an extremity in up to 10 healthy adult volunteers. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
General:
- Age >18 years
- Written informed consent following appropriate study information
- Ability to understand the nature, significance, and implications of the study and to comply with study-related instructions
- Willingness and ability to attend the scheduled study visit and local follow-up assessment
For healthy volunteers:
- No known chronic inflammatory or infectious skin disease
- Clinically unaffected skin at the intended application site
For patients with atopic dermatitis:
- Physician-confirmed diagnosis of atopic dermatitis
- At least one lesional skin site suitable for measurement
- Stable clinical condition allowing a single application of the microneedle patch
For patients with chronic wounds:
- Chronic ulcer present for at least 3 months
- Physician-confirmed wound diagnosis
- Wound-margin area suitable for application of the microneedle patch
- No clinical signs of an acute wound infection requiring treatment
Exclusion criteria:
- Known hypersensitivity to components of the microneedle patch or to the fixation or disinfection materials used
- Clinically relevant coagulation disorder or therapeutic anticoagulation, if the investigator considers this to be associated with an increased risk of bleeding
- Marked immunosuppression or other conditions associated with a clinically relevant increased risk of infection
- Acute febrile illness or severe systemic disease
- Concurrent participation in another study, if this may affect the safety of the participant or the evaluability of the present study
- Pregnancy or breastfeeding
- Participants under legal supervision or guardianship, including individuals committed to an institution by order of judicial or administrative authorities
- Any other medical or organizational circumstances that, in the investigator’s judgment, preclude safe participation
- Participants who are dependent on the investigator or sponsor, for example medical students at Kiel University (CAU)
